input.quote: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.
input.rationale: There is no exclusivity heading, and § 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other" similar software or services. However, § 3(i) (p0042) imposes a de facto sole-supplier/requirements obligation on Client: every credit report for a borrower underwritten through a System using the Interface must be ordered from TrueLink. That commitment runs for the full term of the Agreement, is not capped at 12 months, and carries no automatic exit if TrueLink misses service levels (e.g. the § 3(b) response-time and § 3(d) availability standards) or delivery dates, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. The shortest cure is to make the sourcing commitment permissive, which reaches the preferred position without disturbing TrueLink's transmission obligations or the surrounding disclaimer.

proposal.summary: Make the credit-report sourcing commitment permissive so Client has no sole-supplier obligation.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3(i) currently requires us to order every credit report from TrueLink for Interface-underwritten borrowers, which is a sole-supplier commitment for the full term with no performance exit. We have made it permissive, consistent with our position that we take on no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; if you need a commitment, we can discuss one limited to a defined category, capped at 12 months and ending automatically on any service-level or delivery failure.

ops.oldText: Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower
ops.newText: Client may order from TrueLink a credit report on any borrower

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
